en.titre: Paintings By Women History Tried To Forget

en.texte: shows the queen fainting before the king she has come to beg for her people's lives. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in the 1620s. In 1616 she had become the first woman admitted to Florence's Academy of Drawing.

was believed to be by Jacques-Louis David when it entered the Met in 1917. Only in 1996 did a historian name the real artist: Marie-Denise Villers. I learned to see the cracked windowpane behind her on Artura, one artwork a day with its story.

en.titre: Vase of Flowers and Conch Shell
en.texte: was painted by Anne Vallayer-Coster, who joined the Royal Academy in 1770, at 26, as a painter of still lifes. Her flowers were so admired that Marie Antoinette became her patron. She painted this one in 1780.

was painted by Berthe Morisot, who showed in seven of the eight Impressionist exhibitions. Her brushstrokes are so loose the woman almost melts into the garden. On her death certificate, her profession was listed as none.
